description: Solo developer and space science enthusiast building TerraAnalog, an interactive mission control atlas utilizing NASA open data to evaluate Earth analog sites for lunar and Martian habitats.
summary: TerraAnalog is an interactive mission control atlas and spatial telemetry console that evaluates Earth-based analog sites (Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater, Mauna Loa Lava Tubes, and McMurdo Dry Valleys) against lunar and Martian conditions across 5 key environmental axes to optimize future habitat planning using NASA open data.
details:
TerraAnalog: Earth-to-Space Habitat Explorer is an interactive atlas and telemetry interface which compares earth analog environments such as the Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater, Mauna Loa Lava Tubes and McMurdo Dry Valleys to lunar and Martian environments.

The interface includes an orbital map, 5 axis data comparison (Temperature, Aridity, Regolith Composition, UV Radiation and Topography) and a Mission Profile Matcher which helps to identify the best possible sites on Earth to simulate missions.

The project uses real world data from NASA Earthdata, POWER, Mars Trek, Moon Trek and rover data.

HTML5, CSS3/Tailwind and JavaScript have been used to create this interactive project which can be viewed live on GitHub Pages.

This product has been created out of creativity to help bridge the gap between testing on earth and preparing for deep space missions. This has significantly sped up the process of finding habitat locations for future Artemis and Mars missions.
